# 12 Refractory gold in sulphides

> How do two gold carriers with different floatability share the recovery?

Gold locked in pyrite and arsenopyrite that no grind can free; flotation makes a sulphide concentrate for oxidation downstream, so sulphide recovery is gold recovery.

| Case id | Category | Circuit family | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `refractory_gold` | integration | rougher | authored scenario; parameters inside cited ranges; not plant-calibrated |

Open it in the workbench: [https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/?case=refractory_gold](https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/?case=refractory_gold); on its own stage: [focus](https://oreflow.ml.fasl-work.com/focus/refractory_gold).

## The problem

The concentrate goes to roasting or pressure oxidation, so the flotation circuit is judged by sulphide recovery at a mass pull the oxidation plant can take.

The two carriers float differently, arsenopyrite more slowly, so the case asks how they share the recovery and where the slower one is lost.

## The ore

| Mineral | Role | Mass fraction | Liberation size | Composite content | Host | Separation response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pyrite | Au carrier (trace) | 0.045 | 120 µm | 0.45 | Quartz and silicate gangue | flotation |
| Arsenopyrite | Au carrier (trace) | 0.012 | 80 µm | 0.40 | Quartz and silicate gangue | flotation |
| Quartz and silicate gangue | gangue | the balance | - | - | - | flotation |

| Payable | Head grade | Carried by |
|---|---|---|
| Au | 2.20 g/t | Pyrite (55%, trace); Arsenopyrite (45%, trace) |

Bond ball-mill work index 18.0 kWh/t; crushing work index 19.5 kWh/t.

## The six variants

Each variant changes exactly one input of the nominal state.

| Variant | Change | Recovery of the primary payable | Concentrate grade | Specific energy, total | Product P80 | Mill power | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nominal design | - | 94.2% | 28.1 g/t | 19.53 kWh/t | 106 µm | 5,643 kW | - |
| Harder ore (+25% work index) | Bond work index: 18.0 kWh/t to 22.5 kWh/t (x1.25) | 91.5% | 27.5 g/t | 21.98 kWh/t | 127 µm | 6,300 kW | `power_limited` |
| Coarser grind target (+35% P80) | Grind target (P80): 106 µm to 143 µm (x1.35) | 89.0% | 27.1 g/t | 16.36 kWh/t | 143 µm | 4,660 kW | - |
| Higher throughput (+25%) | Ore throughput: 310 t/h to 388 t/h (x1.25) | 88.9% | 27.8 g/t | 17.59 kWh/t | 127 µm | 6,300 kW | `power_limited` |
| More collector (+60%) | Collector dose: 60.0 g/t to 96.0 g/t (x1.60) | 95.1% | 28.0 g/t | 19.53 kWh/t | 106 µm | 5,643 kW | - |
| More air (+40% gas velocity) | Gas velocity (rougher): 1.40 cm/s to 1.96 cm/s (x1.40) | 95.2% | 28.0 g/t | 19.53 kWh/t | 106 µm | 5,643 kW | - |

- **Harder ore (+25% work index).** Bond work index 25% higher. The circuit needs more energy per tonne for the same grind; where the installed power runs out the mill runs at its limit and the product coarsens, which then costs liberation.
- **Coarser grind target (+35% P80).** Grind target 35% coarser. Less energy per tonne and fewer liberated grains, so the concentrate grade falls; a flotation circuit pays for the energy saved in recovery as well, while magnetic drums keep capturing the coarser composites and recover a little more iron at the lower grade.
- **Higher throughput (+25%).** Throughput 25% higher. Once the mill reaches its installed power the grind coarsens, and in a flotation circuit the residence in every bank falls in proportion as well; the metal recovered per hour can still rise, because the extra tonnes outweigh the recovery lost.
- **More collector (+60%).** More collector. The valuable mineral's response saturates at a lower dose than the gangue's and the composites', so extra reagent adds recovery with diminishing returns and floats more of what dilutes the concentrate.
- **More air (+40% gas velocity).** Gas velocity 40% higher. A larger bubble surface area flux raises every rate constant; the froth also recovers more water, which carries more entrained gangue, but the faster flotation of the valuable mineral usually weighs more, so recovery rises and the grade holds or rises slightly.

## At the nominal state

| Check | Value | Plausible range | Within |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recovery of the primary payable | 94.2% | 80.0% to 95.0% | yes |
| Concentrate grade | 28.1 g/t | 12.0 g/t to 60.0 g/t | yes |

Every unit and the circuit close within 2.0e-13 relative (the requirement is 1e-9). Water: 2.26 m³/t.

## Method records at the nominal state

- **Optimizer:** optimal at Grind target (P80) 89 µm, Collector dose 180.0 g/t, Gas velocity (rougher) 2.50 cm/s; active constraint: power; recovered metal +4.15% against the nominal state (110 engine runs from 6 starts).
- **Uncertainty** (128 Latin-hypercube samples of the ore): recovery P05 90.2%, P50 94.1%, P95 96.0%; probability of meeting every constraint 80%.
- **Sobol indices** (1536 engine runs), the input with the largest total index: recovery of the primary payable: floatability (total index 0.90); concentrate grade: head grade (total index 0.94); specific energy, grinding: work index (total index 1.00); recovered primary payable: head grade (total index 0.97).
- **Kinetic fits:** of the five lumped models fitted to the virtual batch test, the gamma model projects the rougher bank closest to the exact bank recovery by true flotation (94.9%), 0.48 points below it.

## Scope and assumptions

Gold is a trace element in each carrier with a declared share; its recovery follows the carriers' recovery.

Concentrate grade and mass pull are ore specific; the case is authored and labelled as such.

## Reading it in the workbench

Separation: recovery by size of the payable combines both carriers.

Methods, Sobol sensitivity: floatability is the dominant source of the spread in recovery.

## Sources

- **breakage:** Moly-Cop Tools energy-specific selection (alpha0 0.0091 t/kWh, alpha1 0.651, alpha2 2.5, d_crit 6514 µm) and its documented alternative breakage set (beta0 0.4, beta1 0.65, beta2 4.02); dossier section 1.4.
- **crusher:** Whiten classification K1 0.5 to 0.95 CSS, K2 1.7 to 3.5 CSS, K3 about 2.3; dossier section 1.3.
- **cyclone:** Plitt geometry ratios typical of mineral-processing cyclones; sharpness and underflow density authored; dossier section 2.
- **flotation:** k from bubble surface area flux (Gorain et al. 1997), Savassi entrainment, perfect-mixer banks; floatability and widths authored within Trahar (1981) size behaviour; dossier section 3.
- **collector:** Saturating collector response with gangue saturating at higher dose (chalcopyrite/pyrite critical review, PMC9572913); dossier section 3.5.
- **water:** Process-water capacity per tonne of ore (pumping and thickener capacity), authored 5% above each case's nominal requirement; it is the water constraint of the operating-point optimizer.
- **kpi:** Nominal KPI ranges are typical practice ranges from the dossier section 3.7 and the cited sources; they are plausibility gates, not predictions.
